Written 2026-09-04. Work top to bottom — **the order is load-bearing.** Each
task leaves the state the next one needs, and the tasks that destroy a household
come last. Running them out of order means rebuilding the fixture.

Tick the Result column as you go. Record what actually happened, including
"as expected" — an untouched column a week later is indistinguishable from a
test that was skipped.

---

## Stop. Read this first.

**There is one environment and it holds one live household.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **PROTECT — never target** | `TooFat&TooCurious` |
| Its id | `5065fb0a-3861-4232-ac38-24a3dfa501b0` |
| Its owner | `e448f408-a001-70ad-d17c-2a8350e0f505` (mike.akram@gmail.com) |
| Also protect | `polina.tsaliev@gmail.com` — the second live account |

Every task below deletes something. Before any destructive step, confirm the
household id you are acting on is **not** the one above. The app does not ask
twice; these tests are the first time several of these paths run at all.

Sign the test accounts in on the **Simulator**, and keep your iPhone signed in
to the real account — that way a mistap cannot reach the live household from the
device most likely to be picked up out of habit.

---

## Do you need a third device?

**No.** You need three *accounts*, not three devices, and those are different
things.

Only one task needs two clients acting at literally the same moment — the invite
race in **T3** — and Simulator plus your iPhone already covers that. Everywhere
else, signing out and back in on the same device is exactly equivalent, because
the server cannot tell the difference and the server is what is under test.

If you want three concurrent sessions anyway, **boot a second Simulator** rather
than finding a third phone: macOS runs multiple simulators side by side, so
Simulator ×2 + iPhone gives three live clients for free.

**Accounts** — Gmail plus-addressing, all landing in your normal inbox:

| Alias | Role in the run |
|---|---|
| `mike.akram+t1@gmail.com` | **A** — creates the household, owner |
| `mike.akram+t2@gmail.com` | **B** — joins, outlives the owner |
| `mike.akram+t3@gmail.com` | **C** — joins, gets removed, rejoins, deletes |

Passwords must now be 8+ characters with a lowercase letter and a number.

## T0 — Build the fixture

Nothing is being tested here. This is the household everything else consumes.

| # | Step |
|---|---|
| 1 | Sign up **A** on Simulator. Create household — name it `LIFECYCLE-TEST` so it is unmistakable in any table scan |
| 2 | Add a store with a real aisle layout, and put **at least 6 items** on the list — a few `ACTIVE`, a few moved to suggestions |
| 3 | Complete one shopping session, so there are `Commit` rows and trip history |
| 4 | Invite **B**, join on iPhone. Invite **C**, join on Simulator (sign A out first, or use the second Simulator) |
| 5 | Have **each** of the three add at least one item, so every member owns some data |

**Record before you break anything** — you will compare against this at the end:

```bash
H=<LIFECYCLE-TEST household id>
AWS_PROFILE=mine aws dynamodb query --region us-east-1 \
  --table-name "GroceryItem-vdsfrt2plzgwfdae2ucpxtwzh4-NONE" \
  --index-name groceryItemsByHouseholdIdAndStatus \
  --key-condition-expression "householdId = :h" \
  --expression-attribute-values "{\":h\":{\"S\":\"$H\"}}" --select COUNT
```

**Baseline captured 2026-09-04 16:2x UTC.** Household is `TestHousehold`, not

## T1 — Owner removes a member

**Path:** `remove`. Owner-only. **Never run before.**

| # | Step | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | As **A**, remove **C** | Succeeds |
| 2 | As **C**, without signing out, pull to refresh | **Access denied immediately** — not when the token expires |
| 3 | As **C**, force-quit and reopen | Sees no household |
| 4 | As **A**, check the list | C's items are **still there** |
| 5 | Try the same removal as **B** | Refused — not the owner |

```bash
# C must be gone from the group, and the group must still hold A and B
AWS_PROFILE=mine aws cognito-idp list-users-in-group \
  --user-pool-id us-east-1_OIBNTn0XB --group-name "$H" --region us-east-1 \
  --query 'Users[].Username'
```

| Check | Pass | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C loses access without re-auth | | |
| C's items survive | | |
| C out of the Cognito group, A and B still in | | |
| Non-owner cannot remove | | |

::: {.callout-note}
Step 2 is the real test. Group removal revokes the claim, but a token already
issued still carries the old groups until it refreshes. If C can still read for
minutes afterwards, that is a finding, not a flake — note how long.
:::

## T2 — Member leaves and rejoins

**Path:** colour reassignment and group re-grant. **Never run before.**

| # | Step | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | As **A**, generate a new invite code | Old one is dead |
| 2 | **C** rejoins with it | In, with a colour |
| 3 | Note every member's colour | Three distinct |
| 4 | As **C**, leave the household | Household intact, A and B unaffected |
| 5 | As **B**, add an item while C is away | Succeeds |
| 6 | Generate another code; **C** rejoins again | **C's colour does not collide** with A's or B's |

| Check | Pass | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rejoin restores group membership | | |
| Colour is distinct from both remaining members | | |
| C's earlier items still attributed to C | | |

## T3 — Two people race one invite code

**Path:** `consumeInviteCode`'s conditional write. **The only task needing two
devices at once.**

Needs a fourth account (`+t4`) since C is already in. Sign up **D** first, then
sign C out to a fresh install state so both are sitting on the join screen.

| # | Step |
|---|---|
| 1 | As **A**, generate a code. Do **not** let anyone use it |
| 2 | Get **C** on one device and **D** on the other, both with the code typed in, join button unpressed |
| 3 | Press both **as close to simultaneously as you can manage** |

| Check | Pass | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Exactly one** gets in | | |
| The loser sees the single generic refusal — not a different message revealing the code was real | | |
| Member count is 3, never 4 | | |

::: {.callout-tip}
Hard to hit by hand. Three or four attempts with a fresh code each time is
reasonable; if it never races, say so rather than marking it passed. A
near-miss still proves single-use.
:::

## T4 — Member deletes their account, others remain

**Path:** `deleteAccount` with a **populated** household. Never run — the only
prior verification was an account with no household at all, which is the least
interesting branch.

Use whichever of C or D is currently in.

| # | Step | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Note their item count and the household total | |
| 2 | Settings → Danger Zone → Delete my account | Completes |
| 3 | As **A**, refresh | Their **items remain**; member count drops by one |
| 4 | Try to sign in as the deleted account | Rejected — user gone |

```bash
AWS_PROFILE=mine aws cognito-idp list-users --user-pool-id us-east-1_OIBNTn0XB \
  --region us-east-1 --query 'Users[].Attributes[?Name==`email`].Value' --output text
# household must still exist, with its items
AWS_PROFILE=mine aws dynamodb get-item --region us-east-1 \
  --table-name "Household-vdsfrt2plzgwfdae2ucpxtwzh4-NONE" \
  --key "{\"id\":{\"S\":\"$H\"}}" --query 'Item.id.S'
```

| Check | Pass | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Cognito user gone | | |
| `User` row gone | | |
| Household **still exists** | | |
| Item count unchanged from baseline | | |
| Out of the Cognito group | | |
| Log shows `account.deleted` with `householdDeleted: false` | | |

::: {.callout-important}
This is the branch that shares `deleteHouseholdData` with `leave`. If the
household disappears here, stop the run and say so — that is the catastrophic
case the new guard exists to prevent.
:::

## T6 — Last member deletes their account

**Path:** the full `deleteHouseholdData` cascade via `deleteAccount`, plus the
new `householdGroupIsEmpty` guard. **The most destructive code in the app, on
the branch that has never run.**

**B is now alone.** Confirm that before proceeding.

| # | Step | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Re-record the item / commit / store counts | Non-zero — the point is watching them go |
| 2 | As **B**, Settings → Danger Zone → Delete my account | Completes |

```bash
for T in GroceryItem Commit HouseholdStore; do
  echo -n "$T: "
  AWS_PROFILE=mine aws dynamodb scan --region us-east-1 \
    --table-name "$T-vdsfrt2plzgwfdae2ucpxtwzh4-NONE" \
    --filter-expression "householdId = :h" \
    --expression-attribute-values "{\":h\":{\"S\":\"$H\"}}" --select COUNT \
    --query 'Count' --output text
done
AWS_PROFILE=mine aws dynamodb get-item --region us-east-1 \
  --table-name "Household-vdsfrt2plzgwfdae2ucpxtwzh4-NONE" \
  --key "{\"id\":{\"S\":\"$H\"}}"
AWS_PROFILE=mine aws cognito-idp get-group --user-pool-id us-east-1_OIBNTn0XB \
  --group-name "$H" --region us-east-1
```

| Check | Pass | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `GroceryItem` count → 0 | | |
| `Commit` count → 0 | | |
| `HouseholdStore` count → 0 | | |
| Household row gone | | |
| Cognito group gone (`ResourceNotFoundException`) | | |
| Cognito user gone | | |
| Log shows `account.deleted` with `householdDeleted: true` | | |
| **No** `household.deleteRefused` in the logs | | |
| `TooFat&TooCurious` untouched | | |

::: {.callout-note}
`ProductAisleMapping` is **expected** to survive — it hangs off `storeId`, not
`householdId`, so the cascade cannot reach it. It is inert without its store.
Documented behaviour, not a failure.
:::

---

## The guard, tested deliberately

`householdGroupIsEmpty` refuses to delete unless the member-count index **and**
the Cognito group both say the household is empty. T6 proves the happy path —
both agree, deletion proceeds. This proves it actually blocks.

| # | Step |
|---|---|
| 1 | Build a throwaway household with two members, E and F |
| 2 | Remove **E's** `User` row directly in DynamoDB, leaving them in the Cognito group — simulating the index having lost a member it should still show |
| 3 | As **F**, delete your account |

| Check | Pass | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Household is **not** deleted | | |
| Log shows `household.deleteRefused` with `reason: cognito_group_still_populated` | | |

Then confirm the IAM half, which `tsc` cannot see:

| Check | Pass | Result |
|---|---|---|
| No `household.deleteRefused` with `reason: group_check_failed` anywhere in T6 | | |

A `group_check_failed` means the `cognito-idp:ListUsersInGroup` grant did not
deploy. The guard fails closed, so the symptom is households surviving that
should have been deleted — safe, but wrong, and invisible without this check.
